newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amcoal expects higher second half earnings.
newsitem.headline: Amcoal expects higher second half earnings.

text.p: Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd said it expected higher earnings in the second of the year to end-March, assuming the present weaker rand/dollar exchange continued.

"Assuming the present weaker rand/U.S. dollar exchange rate continues, it is forecast that earnings for the second half of the year will be higher than those of the first half," chairman David Rankin said in a statement.
The company reported earnings up 34.3 percent to 434.1 million rand in the six months to September 30 1996.
Rankin said export sales were expected to remain largely unchanged in the second half of the year, although some improvement in sales to the domestic market was anticipated.
Export sales of coal were marginally higher at 7.19 million tonnes in the six months to September 30 from 7.16 million tonnes in the same period a year ago.

Sales to electricity utility Eskom fell to 15.98 million tonnes from 16.78 million tonnes due to a disappointing performance at New Denmark Colliery. Steps to improve output from this colliery were being implemented, Rankin said.
